newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Best on Ground-Andrew Bartram's Aussie Rules Column.
newsitem.headline: Best on Ground-Andrew Bartram's Aussie Rules Column.

text.p: By Andrew Bartram*
A LESSON FOR THE ARL
State against state, mate against mate is how the Australian Rugby League (ARL) promotes its annual three-match state of origin series between New South Wales and Queensland.

The ARL might reconsider its push into the AFL heartland after friends and relatives, and a handful of spectators numbering just 25,000, turned up at the MCG on Wednesday night to witness one of League's premier events.
Here in Melbourne, the AFL heartland, a good Aussie rules player can attract a bigger crowd to a supermarket opening.
BACKMAN BARRED

Talented but wayward backman Aaron James was suspended indefinitely by Collingwood for the fourth public indiscretion in his short career after an incident involving two women at a South Yarra bar on Sunday.
A club source said James had earlier been upset by the apparent refusal of some team mates to kick the ball to him in the match against Richmond two nights earlier.
CROWN JEWELS SAGA
Geelong on-baller Garry Hocking was upset when Footscray's Brad Wira squeezed his testicles during the Optus Oval clash last Saturday.
Hocking was reported for retailiating and later upset Wira when he told the tribunal what happened.
The Bulldog was suspended for two matches, Hocking one.
PUNTERS SEEN WARY OF BAD WEATHER
A round of unpredictable results last week upset self-respecting tipsters too. A few more look likely with rain expected in most football states at the weekend.
Last-start winners Sydney and Richmond meet at the SCG tonight in a match with the incentive for the winner being a likely spot in the top eight.

The Swans, who have played only three games at home this year, will take time adjusting to the smaller ground but should defeat the inconsistent Tigers, who haven't strung two wins together in nine matches.
Pace-setters the Western Bulldogs host Port Adelaide at Optus Oval on Saturday.

The Bulldogs look almost unbackable at home and despite expected soggy conditions should be too strong for the Power, who have been destablised by an internal feud between coach John Cahill and football manager Mick Moylan.
Collingwood and West Coast meet in a must-win game for both clubs at Victoria Park on Saturday.
Despite boasting one win between them in their past three matches, both teams remain in the top five and the loser could drop out of the top eight.
Collingwood with the home ground advantage and the support of a sometimes hostile crowd should get the points.
Hawthorn will not be daunted by the trip to Geelong, having won twice in their last three visits to Kardinia Park.

Saturday's assignment against the rebounding Cats is a difficult one, especially without in-form fullback Mark Graham. But the confident Hawks should have the midfield edge, giving their forwards enough chances to kick a winning score.
Fremantle have their best chance of beating an injury-hit Essendon for the first time at home at Subiaco Oval on Sunday.
The Dockers look relatively settled and should beat the Bombers who have made at least six forced changes.
Bookmakers have backed St Kilda to beat Carlton at Waverley Park on Sunday.
The Saints are coming off a good away win over the Eagles and have a perceived edge in pace over the ageing Blues.
Rain will make for an even contest but the Blues who have won their past four matches, should sneak home.
Skipper Wayne Carey makes his much-awaited return to the North Melbourne team after a shoulder reconstruction for the clash with Adelaide at Football Park on on Sunday.
Don't be surprised if the King is a late withdrawal and his return is delayed until after next weekend's state games.
North would be foolish to risk their match-winner against the in-form Crows, who are currently close to unbeatable at home and should add last year's premiers to their list of victims.
Brisbane's season rides on the result of Sunday's game against Melbourne at the MCG.
If the Lions are to be in the September action they must beat the Demons who, under caretaker coach Greg Hutchinson, have been competitive but hardly threatening.
The Lions have more at stake and should win.
*Andrew Bartram is a freelance sports writer who will be writing a regular AFL column for Reuters.
-- Reuters Melbourne Bureau 61-3 9286-1435
